title: Automated ASPECTS scoring for acute ischemic stroke
summary: Assist clinicians by calculating ASPECTS from brain imaging and presenting an explainable result.
description:
Clinical Motivation

In acute stroke, time is brain. Clinicians must decide within a narrow window whether a patient qualifies for thrombolysis or thrombectomy, and that decision hinges partly on ASPECTS (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score), a 10-point score radiologists compute manually under time pressure from a non-contrast CT (NCCT). Each of 10 predefined regions in the middle-cerebral-artery territory - caudate, lentiform nucleus, insula, internal capsule, and M1-M6 - is inspected for early ischemic change; one point is deducted per affected region. The process is subjective, reader-dependent, and slow at exactly the moment speed matters most.

The Challenge

Build an end-to-end system that estimates ASPECTS from an NCCT head scan: detect early ischemic change such as loss of grey-white differentiation or subtle hypodensity, localize it to the correct ASPECTS regions, and output a 0-10 score. A system that does one objective well but ignores the other is incomplete.

Objective 1 - Ischemic Change Detection (the ML core)

On NCCT, detect and segment areas of early ischemic change. The signal may be only a few Hounsfield units rather than a bright bleed. Hemispheric symmetry is the strongest cue because the healthy contralateral side is a built-in reference. Left-right symmetry analysis and contralateral density comparison are encouraged, and a rule-based plus ML hybrid is legitimate.

Objective 2 - ASPECTS Region Localization and Scoring

Map the 10 ASPECTS regions onto the patient scan and derive the score. Pre-built ASPECTS region atlases in standard space may be used. The atlas must be registered robustly onto each native NCCT despite varying head tilt, slice thickness, and skull stripping, because a naive rigid fit can misassign regions. Keep final scoring rule-based and explainable by comparing per-region HU values with the contralateral side. Registration toolkits may include ANTs, elastix, SimpleITK, or a learned method such as VoxelMorph.

The Interface Between Them (where systems break)

The two objectives must connect: detected change has to land in the correct region after registration. Consider the shared coordinate frame, how registration error propagates into wrong region assignments, and how a small detection near a region boundary is handled.

Datasets

APIS (primary): a public paired NCCT and ADC-MRI dataset for acute ischemic stroke, with NCCT lesion labels derived from MRI. It contains approximately 60 training pairs and 36 test pairs and is available by registration. AISD (secondary) contains 397 NCCT scans with DWI-confirmed lesion masks, including 345 training and 52 test scans. ISLES 2018 is CT-perfusion and ISLES 2022 is MRI-only; use them only as reference material because neither provides NCCT ASPECTS labels.

ASPECTS Atlas and Registration Resources (for Objective 2)

An NCCT ASPECTS atlas with 10 labeled regions, atlas files on Figshare, the MIPLAB elderly NCCT/FLAIR atlas, a whole-brain stroke-population CT-MRI atlas, and published atlas-based scoring methods may be used as registration and validation resources.

Deliverables

A pipeline that takes an NCCT volume and returns: (a) a segmentation or heatmap of detected ischemic change, (b) a per-region ischemic-change flag across the 10 ASPECTS regions, and (c) an overall ASPECTS score. Include a visualization overlaying both the detected change and the 10 region boundaries on the CT.

title: AI-guided windshield installation
summary: Guide operators through windshield fitment with real-time visual feedback and pressure-point verification.
description:
Problem Context

The windshield installation process is performed manually on the vehicle assembly line. Operators must apply pressure across the windshield according to defined standard operating procedures for proper sealing and adhesion. Missed or incorrectly applied pressure can result in inconsistent fitment, loose installation, water leakage, noise or vibration issues, and increased rework.

Problem Statement

Build an AI-powered Windshield Installation Guidance System that provides real-time visual feedback during fitment. Cameras and computer vision should identify the windshield area, display predefined pressure application points on a monitor or augmented display, guide operators to apply adequate pressure sequentially, track completion of every required point, and confirm when the standard process is complete.

What You May Build

A computer-vision solution that identifies the windshield and guides operators through predefined pressure points; an intelligent vision system that detects missed points, incomplete sequences, or incorrect patterns; an AI agent that analyses installation data, operator actions, compliance records, recurring quality issues, and training needs; or an augmented-reality solution that overlays pressure locations directly onto the windshield.

Suggested Technical Stack

Computer vision
Real-time tracking system
Agentic AI or multi-agent systems
Web application

title: AI-powered assembly inspection
summary: Verify manufacturing assembly quality with computer vision, AI, and optional wearable AR.
description:
Problem Context

Assembly quality verification often depends on manual visual inspections of wiring assemblies, connectors, fasteners, clips, and other components. Manual inspection is susceptible to human error, fatigue, inspection variability, and inconsistency across shifts. Missed defects such as incorrect routing, unsecured components, missing fasteners, or unintended contact can lead to rework, production delays, warranty costs, and reduced product reliability.

Problem Statement

Build an AI-powered Assembly Inspection System that combines computer vision, artificial intelligence, and optional wearable AR devices to automate assembly verification and quality inspection. Real-time image analysis should compare live assembly conditions against approved digital standards and identify incorrect routing, missing fastening elements, improper component positioning, or interference risks. Inspection results should be visualized through AR overlays so operators can identify and resolve issues within their field of view.

What You May Build

A real-time computer-vision inspection solution; an AI quality verification engine comparing production images with digital reference models; an AR guidance system showing inspection results, assembly instructions, and defect locations; an AI agent analysing inspection records, defect trends, production data, and operator performance; or a digital traceability platform recording outcomes, classifications, images, compliance metrics, and corrective actions.

Suggested Technical Stack

Computer vision
Real-time tracking system
Agentic AI or multi-agent systems
Web or mobile application
3D modelling
AR/VR

title: AI manufacturing operations assistant
summary: Help factory teams understand constraints, validate plans, detect risks, and keep production moving.
description:
Problem Context

Modern manufacturing plants generate large amounts of real-time information about material shortages, inventory availability, production flow, and operational constraints. This information is spread across emails, messages, sensors, and different software systems. Production planners must manually monitor these inputs, validate schedules, identify bottlenecks, manage exceptions, and take corrective action. The process is time-consuming, reactive, and dependent on human expertise.

Problem Statement

Build an AI-powered Manufacturing Operations Assistant that monitors real-time factory data, understands operational constraints, validates production plans, detects risks, and recommends corrective actions to keep production running smoothly. AI agents should collect information from multiple sources, analyse factory conditions, identify material shortages or production bottlenecks, and provide actionable recommendations to planners and operators. The system should support faster decisions, reduce manual effort, improve production efficiency, and increase operational reliability.

What You May Build

An AI agent that gathers information from emails, chats, reports, or factory systems and converts it into structured insights; an intelligent planning assistant that validates production schedules; predictive monitoring for bottlenecks, congestion, shortages, or flow disruptions; a recommendation engine for corrective actions and recovery plans; or an autonomous multi-agent decision-support platform for real-time factory operations.

Suggested Technical Stack

Generative AI and LLMs
Agentic AI or multi-agent systems
Machine learning and predictive analysis
Natural language processing (NLP)
